newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Gowda says Bhutto dismissal an internal affair.
newsitem.headline: Gowda says Bhutto dismissal an internal affair.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday the removal of Pakistan's Benazir Bhutto was an internal affair that will not affect the two countries' ties.
He said in a statement from Zimbabwe where he is attending a Third World Group of 15 (G-15) trade summit that India would continue its policy of maintaining good neighbourly relations.
"We see these events as Pakistan's internal developments and are following them closely," Gowda said in the brief statement.
"India has always been keen to maintain good neighbourly relations with Pakistan. This policy continues," he said.
Deve Gowda and his foreign minister, Inder Gujral, were unavailable for further comment.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars in the nearly five decades they have been independent from Britain and they have not held officials talks for more than two years.

Pakistani President Farooq Leghari dismissed prime minister Bhutto's government on Tuesday, accusing it of corruption and misrule in what appears to have been a planned action that had army support and was within his constitutional powers.
